# Ether plugin reference

> Build EPP/1 plugins with the exact shipped manifest, SDK and host-service contracts.

Generated by go generate ./internal/plugins/devreference. Do not edit generated files.
Developer documentation and API vocabulary are in English. Capabilities describe behavior; permissions grant access. Hosted QuickJS is not Node.

## Getting started

Get a first result with [Start here in 5 minutes](/plugins/reference/five-minutes), or explore [ten authoring recipes](/plugins/reference/agent-recipes).

Build the smallest plugin that answers one useful question. Start with Plugins → Add plugin → Code, select a Studio template, and run its preview before installing. A plugin adds a source, integration, notification channel, live TV source, extension, or whole content library.

## Choose a runtime
Hosted TypeScript runs inside QuickJS on wazero. There is no Node filesystem, process, environment, or direct networking. Use the permission-checked host services. Export `handle(request)` and return `{status, headers?, body}`. Calls on the hosted `ether` global are synchronous. SDK clients may be asynchronous in a sidecar; use `await` in portable SDK code.

Remote plugins run in your own process and serve HTTP or dial an outbound authenticated WebSocket tunnel. Their OS permissions are your responsibility. A remote plugin cannot use hosted folder grants or SecretGet; configuration is delivered through the remote configuration flow.

## First hosted handler
```ts
export function handle(req) {
  if (req.path === '/ether/health')
    return { status: 200, body: { status: 'ok' } };
  if (req.path === '/ether/test')
    return { status: 200, body: { ok: true, message: 'Ready' } };
  return { status: 404, body: { error: 'Unknown route' } };
}
```

Use [Manifest](/plugins/reference/manifest) to declare identity and runtime, [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities) to declare behavior, then [Testing](/plugins/reference/testing) before distributing a package. Expand the generated declarations on each page for exact signatures, limits, and validation errors. The Go validator is authoritative where optional wire fields have conditional requirements.

## Start here in 5 minutes

Your first result is a catalogue containing The Matrix. You need an Ether development server you control, its admin token, and the Ether CLI from this checkout. No provider account or media download is needed. The sample describes a movie; playback still needs an owner-configured playable source.

## 1. Create a plugin (one minute)
From the repository root, build the CLI once if it is not already on your PATH:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o ./ether ./cmd/ether
./ether plugin new catalogue --lang ts ./my-first-plugin
```

Open `my-first-plugin/src/index.ts` and find the `/catalog/` branch. It returns a real Stremio `metas` entry with an IMDb ID, type and name. The manifest declares the matching `featured` catalogue and a list source named Featured picks. Change the reverse-DNS plugin ID in the manifest before distributing your own project.

## 2. Get a green check (one minute)

```sh
./ether plugin check ./my-first-plugin
./ether plugin test ./my-first-plugin
```

Expect `PASS`. Errors name the field or route to fix and link to its reference topic. For an agent, use `./ether plugin check --json ./my-first-plugin`. All generated templates work without npm dependencies. The check is offline; your local server is used only in the next step.

## 3. Install and keep the loop open (one minute)
Set `ETHER_TOKEN` in your shell to your local server's admin token, then run:

```sh
./ether plugin dev ./my-first-plugin --server http://localhost:32400
```

Use your development server's actual port if it differs. Expect `Reloaded community.example.myfirstplugin` followed by `Watching`. The watcher checks conformance before installing each saved change and prints plugin logs. If a save fails, fix the reported field and save again; the watcher stays open. Ctrl-C stops it. A 401/403 means the token or grants need attention; a connection error means the server address or process needs attention.

## 4. See your result (one minute)
In that server's console, open Plugins and enable your plugin after reviewing its permissions. Open Collections → New collection. In Sources, choose Featured picks from your plugin, replacing the default catalogue source if present. Keep the media type Movies. The collection preview resolves the sample's IMDb ID to The Matrix in your Ether catalogue. If it is missing, confirm the plugin is enabled and that your development catalogue contains that title; the sample does not populate Ether's TMDB catalogue itself.

For an immediate plugin-owned page without catalogue matching, scaffold `extension` instead of `catalogue`, install it with the same dev command, then open its Language overview page from the plugin. Its ViewSpec displays the sample active language, `en`.

## 5. Make it yours and share it (one minute)
Edit the catalogue response, save, and re-open the collection preview. Keep IDs stable and page larger results. Put configuration in `settings.schema.json`, labels in `i18n/en.json`, and secrets in sealed settings rather than source. When the result looks right:

```sh
./ether plugin pack -o ./my-first-plugin.etherpkg ./my-first-plugin
./ether plugin check ./my-first-plugin.etherpkg
```

Upload that package through Plugins → Add plugin on another development server. See [the authoring recipes](/plugins/reference/agent-recipes) for ten directions to take next, [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities) for route shapes, and [Testing](/plugins/reference/testing) for the limits of offline checks.

## Recipes for humans and coding agents

Start with one useful response, then build the next thing you want to use. The guide below covers ten plugin types, exact CLI commands, manifest decisions, host-service permissions, and common repairs. Use the header’s Copy for your AI assistant button to copy all chapters and generated contracts, or give your agent `/ether/plugins/reference/llms.txt` on this server. Hosted code has no Node filesystem or npm resolution; use the shipped host-service contracts and bundle imports.

## Manifest

Every package has `manifest.json`. `id`, `version`, and `name` are required. The native `ether` block requires protocol, kind, and runtime. A manifest without that block is a plain Stremio add-on. Keep reverse-DNS identity stable and increase SemVer for updates.

```json
{"id":"org.example.hello","name":"Hello","version":"0.1.0","ether":{"protocol":1,"kind":"extension","runtime":{"kind":"hosted","entry":"plugin.js"}}}
```

## Reading the generated fields
The schema table lists required fields **within their parent object**, constraints, enum values, and explicitly declared defaults. An optional parent need not be present. Absence of a schema default does not imply zero is the runtime default: consult the Go type comments and validator below. Go field tables describe serialization, not validation requiredness. `omitempty` never proves that a field is optional for your chosen capability.

Network permissions, contribution metadata, settings references, schedules, and runtime entry points are validated together. Errors identify the field to fix. See [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities), [Settings](/plugins/reference/settings), and [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

## Capabilities & contribution routes

Capabilities describe what a plugin does; permissions describe which host data it can use. Declare only the capabilities you implement. Required contribution metadata depends on the capability and plugin kind; the generated validator below enumerates all combinations and errors.

| Capability | Entry point or contribution |
|---|---|
| stream_source | Stremio `/stream/{type}/{id}.json`; lazy streams open through `/ether/open/{id}` |
| debrid_provider | `/ether/debrid/check`, `find`, `acquire`, `link`, `remove`, `account` |
| list_source | `contributes.listSources`; matching Stremio catalogue |
| metadata | Stremio `/meta/{type}/{id}.json` |
| plugin_directory | Plugin directory declarations and discovery routes |
| livetv_channels | `/ether/channels.json`, `/ether/guide/{id}.json`, stream routes |
| subtitles | Stremio subtitles resource; declared languages and formats |
| markers | Declared intro, credits, recap or preview marker kinds |
| notify | Notification metadata; send and send-test handlers |
| events | Explicit event subscriptions and `/ether/events` |
| ranking_step | Deterministic `rank_key(candidate, config)` |
| rule_condition | Deterministic `cond_match(candidate, operator, value)` |
| tools | Declared tool input schema and tool handlers |
| ui | Pages, slots, commands, ViewSpec views and actions |
| onair_content / livetv_pack | Declared On Air segments or TV pack contributions |
| catalog_provider / kind_resolver / matcher | Content kind browse, resolve, match routes |
| frontend_adapter | Authenticated protocol adapter routes |

Reserved capability names cannot be claimed in EPP/1. Ranking and condition hot paths have only log and abort: no I/O, wall clock, or arbitrary host calls. Return a neutral result when there is no useful adjustment. Consult the generated templates and route checks for each response shape rather than inventing one.

## Content kinds & libraries

See the complete content-kind guide below. Start with a bounded browse page, stable external IDs, and a playable leaf. Use [Resolvers](/plugins/reference/resolvers) for bytes and [Folders](/plugins/reference/host-folders) for local files.

## Catalogue sources

A Stremio catalogue returns `{metas:[...]}` for `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json`. The catalogue ID must match `manifest.catalogs` and `ether.contributes.listSources[].catalog`. A list source can appear in collections and home rows; it is different from the signed **plugin marketplace catalogue** described in [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

```json
{"key":"weekly","label":"This week","catalog":"weekly","maxItems":50,"refresh":"1h"}
```

Keep pages bounded, handle search and pagination extras consistently, and use stable metadata IDs. Read parameters from the request; do not return an entire remote library to answer one query. For arbitrary media hierarchies use [Content kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), whose provider sync persists items in Ether's store.

## Resolvers & playback

Resolve only when a viewer requests playback. Browse and metadata must stay cheap. A content-kind resolver returns ordered `sources`; an empty array means temporarily unavailable. File, range, download, direct, container, and release patterns have different ownership of fetching and caching; read the generated PlayableSource types and content-kind guide.

```json
{"sources":[{"id":"primary","pattern":"range","url":"https://media.example.org/track.mp3","mime":"audio/mpeg"}]}
```

Use `{secret:name}` header placeholders instead of returning raw credentials. URLs support only the documented integer placeholders. Return `unavailable` on kind items when an owner needs to see why verified bytes do not exist. Use Ether stream tickets for frontend adapters so media bypasses the plugin process. See [Kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), [Source discovery](/plugins/reference/host-sources), and the native debrid route/error table below.

## Notification channels

`kind: "notification_channel"` with capability `notify` registers a delivery channel. This differs from `ether.notify.owner`, which posts a console notice. Declare `contributes.notification` with `sendTest: true`, supported formats, optional fields, and maximum length. Owners configure channel instances through Notifications.

```json
{"kind":"notification_channel","capabilities":["notify"],"contributes":{"notification":{"sendTest":true,"formats":["text"],"maxLength":1000}}}
```

Implement `POST /ether/notify` (the SDK notify handler). It receives the delivery request, including its test flag for a test send; return the documented NotifyResponse. See the generated router and conformance checks below. Validate channel fields and authenticate external delivery through declared network hosts and secrets. A successful connection test must mean the service accepted the request; do not report success after an upstream error. Never log tokens or signed delivery URLs. The Home Assistant example shows remote notification delivery.

## Settings & setup steps

Declare `ether.settings` inline or as `{"$ref":"settings.schema.json"}`. Referenced files must be in the package. Public values come from `ether.settings.get()` per request; pooled hosted instances restart, so instance memory is not persistent configuration. Read secrets through SecretGet only in hosted code.

```json
{"fields":[{"key":"maxItems","kind":"number","label":"Maximum items"}]}
```

```ts
const maxItems = Number(ether.settings.get().maxItems ?? 12);
// POST /ether/configure validates proposed req.body:
return { status: 200, body: { errors: {} } };
```

Use `$t:key` labels with `ether.strings` and English fallback strings. Dynamic option fields should answer the SDK's options route. `contributes.setup.steps` groups settings fields and optional test routes. `/ether/v1/setup/{step}/test` receives `{step, fields}` and returns `{ok, detail, fields?}`; secrets stay out of that body. Required steps gate content-library sync and visibility until passed or owner-skipped. See the generated SetupStep and settings accessors for exact shapes.

## Events

Subscribe explicitly with capability `events` and `contributes.events.subscribe`. Handle deliveries at `/ether/events`. The generated event constants below are the supported names; unknown names are rejected, not wildcard subscriptions.

```json
{"capabilities":["events"],"contributes":{"events":{"subscribe":["playback.started"]}}}
```

Keep handlers bounded and idempotent using the event ID. A delivery contains the event name, timestamp, optional viewer identity, and payload. Viewer identity is removed unless the live grants allow it. Enabled subscriptions are indexed; nobody subscribing means no plugin event-log work. Avoid polling playback or scanning the library in response to progress events. Use the generated queue and dispatch code to inspect retry behavior and exact envelopes.

## Testing & conformance

Use Studio's run and preview tools while editing. Before distributing, run the offline conformance command on an unpacked package:

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
```

The kit validates manifest fields, package references, owner-facing copy, declared routes, capability response shapes, and hot-path determinism/budgets. Content-kind checks cover pagination termination, page limits, detail round trips, declared live search, and resolver patterns. Shared kind fixtures live in `sdk/conformance/kinds`.

Mock external HTTP, store, viewer, and playback dependencies in SDK tests. Check missing grants, revoked grants, empty results, rate limits, invalid settings, and upstream failures. Offline conformance cannot prove a paid account works: after installation, run the owner's connection test with real credentials. Inspect Studio's calls and logs without exposing secrets. Package only after these checks; see [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

## Packaging & publishing

Bundle hosted SDK imports into the entry artifact. Bare package imports cannot resolve in the hosted virtual filesystem. Put the manifest, referenced settings/strings, and compiled entry into the package; do not include credentials or development caches.

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
ether plugin pack ./my-plugin
```

Keep identity stable and increment version. New permissions require owner review; removing or retyping kind declarations can require explicit replacement approval. Test upgrades and the owner's rollback flow before release.

A marketplace catalogue distributes packages with pinned SHA-256 digests and an Ed25519-signed index. Review every version's permissions, retain revocation reasons, and publish the index and signature together. The catalogue-template guide below describes repository variables, secret key handling, and artifact checks.

## Troubleshooting & errors

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Manifest rejected | Field path and validator message; capability-specific metadata; unsupported names; referenced files |
| Permission denied | Manifest declaration plus current owner grant; a grant may have been revoked since startup |
| Disabled or unavailable | Plugin enabled state, required setup, injected backend availability, saved secrets |
| Network failure | Host allowlist, guarded redirects, private-address protection, body cap, upstream status |
| Folder inaccessible | Hosted runtime, owner-picked root, relative path, symlink containment, revoked grant |
| Hash too large | Use hashStart above 256 MiB; poll until terminal; retry a busy worker later |
| SDK import unresolved | Bundle imports into the hosted entry; do not expect Node resolution in QuickJS |
| Empty library | Setup completion, sync mode, page cursors, declared levels/field types, stable IDs |
| Playback unavailable | Resolver pattern, source URL, secret placeholders, item unavailable reason, viewer access |
| Remote 401 | Plugin credential or tunnel pairing; never substitute a viewer token |
| Rate limited | Honor backoff and bounded work; owner notices allow five per hour |

Generated validators, transport error mapping, and runtime fault definitions below give the exact error messages. Search a message or field name to find its source and relevant type. Keep secrets out of diagnostic output.

## Key/value storage

Plugin-scoped string values survive instance restarts. Missing get returns null in JS; Go also returns a found flag. Use prefixes for list. Remote values are capped at 5 MiB, with the per-plugin quota also enforced. Never store secrets here.

```ts
ether.kv.put("counter", "1");
const value = ether.kv.get("counter");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Public settings

Read current non-secret configuration for each request. No permission declaration is needed for your own public settings. Missing optional settings need a caller-selected default.

```ts
const count = Number(ether.settings.get().maxItems ?? 12);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Sealed secrets

Hosted only. Requires the exact name in permissions.secrets and a saved secret. Missing secrets produce unavailable; undeclared or revoked grants produce permission denied. Remote plugins receive configuration instead.

```ts
const token = ether.secret.get("apiKey");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## HTTP requests

Hosted fetch requires the destination in permissions.network. Redirect destinations are checked too. Read the generated MaxFetchBytes and transport limits; private or blocked destinations fail even if a hostname is declared. Handle upstream non-2xx status explicitly.

```ts
const r = ether.http.fetch({url: "https://api.example.org/status", method: "GET"});
if (r.status !== 200) throw new Error("Service unavailable");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Catalogue lookup

Requires catalog: read. Hosted search clamps invalid limits to 100; get accepts one title ID. SDK and raw global argument shapes differ: use the exact declarations below. Do not scan all titles to answer a single request.

```ts
const titles = ether.catalog.search("Arrival");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Original add-on relay

Hosted drafts imported from a Stremio add-on can ask the original provider while its address stays sealed. It is available only with the draft relay context; ordinary plugins cannot choose arbitrary provider URLs through this service.

```ts
const response = ether.addon.get("/catalog/movie/top.json");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Viewers & watch state

Live viewer grants determine identity, history, and write access. Use granted() before selecting a viewer. History is bounded (host maximum 200). Watch-state writes are journalled and forbidden in read-only tool calls. Never infer authorization from a cached viewer ID.

```ts
const viewers = ether.viewers.granted();
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Collections

Requires collections: write. Writes are journalled and permission-checked on every call. Remote request bodies are capped at 2 MiB. Use stable collection identity for updates. Read-only tool calls cannot mutate state.

```ts
ether.collections.upsert({id: "weekly", name: "Weekly picks", ids: []});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Kind item storage

Requires catalog_provider and your own declared kind. upsert/delete only work for push-mode kinds; pull sync owns its writes. items is cursor-paged. Items are validated against declared levels and fields. Unknown custom fields are dropped; invalid types reject the item.

```ts
const page = ether.kinds.items("recordings", "", 50);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Source discovery

Requires kind_resolver and sources: search or acquire. Search permits indexer discovery and debrid checks; acquire permits opening content. Return a release source after choosing a candidate instead of downloading in the request handler.

```ts
const candidates = ether.sources.resolve({kind: "indexer_search", query: "Example"});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Library blob cache

Cache refs are content addressed blob:<sha256>, never filesystem paths. A library defaults to 2 GiB under a shared min(10 GiB, 5% of cache disk) cap; manifest and owner settings can override it. Remote blob uploads cap at 256 MiB. Use kinds for metadata and cache for bytes.

```ts
const ref = ether.cache.put("library-key", "cover.txt", "hello");
const data = ether.cache.open(ref);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Frontend stream tickets

Mint a scoped, short-lived URL for one of your own kind items. The authenticated viewer must see its library. Embed this URL in the protocol response; Ether serves the bytes without proxying through your plugin. Raw hosted spelling is streamURL; the TypeScript SDK uses streamUrl.

```ts
const url = ether.frontend.streamURL("item-ref");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Storage & folders

Hosted only. Requires folders: read and a live owner-picked root. Paths are relative to the root. Traversal, symlink escapes and revoked grants fail. list/stat return metadata, never contents. hash returns size, Unix modTime, crc32, md5, sha1. Above 256 MiB use hashStart/hashPoll/hashCancel. Only requested files are hashed; unchanged files reuse the guarded digest cache. One active job per plugin, two process-wide; jobs yield while reading and abort if the file changes. See the full kinds guide for job lifecycle and revocation.

```ts
const job = ether.folders.hashStart("picked-root", "album.flac");
const status = ether.folders.hashPoll(job.id);
// Poll later until done, canceled, or error; never busy-loop.
// ether.folders.hashCancel(job.id);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Owner notices

Posts a console notice, limited to five per hour. It does not send through a notification-channel plugin. Read errors and avoid repeated notices on a playback or progress path.

```ts
ether.notify.owner("New recordings are ready");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Logs & abort

Use structured SDK logs or hosted ether.log for bounded diagnostics. Host logs are redacted and rate limited, but do not send secrets in the first place. abort throws a classified aborted fault. Hot-path code has only log and abort.

```ts
ether.log("Refreshing one page");
// ether.abort("Missing required metadata");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Source: docs/plugin-debrid.md

# Native debrid providers

A hosted source plugin may declare `debrid_provider` and
`ether.contributes.source.class: "debrid"`. Its account belongs in secret settings,
read with `ether.secret.get`. It registers automatically with the native debrid
pipeline while enabled; disabling or removing the plugin unregisters it.

The host sends JSON POST requests to these routes:

| Route under `/ether/debrid/` | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | `{hashes: string[]}` | `{cached: Record<string, boolean>}` |
| `find` | `{infoHash}` | `{torrentId}` |
| `acquire` | `{infoHash, magnet, torrentId, cachedOnly}` | `{torrentId, ready, added, files: [{id, path, size, link?}]}` |
| `link` | `{torrentId, fileId, path, link, magnet, infoHash, size}` | `{url, size, expires?}` |
| `remove` | `{torrentId}` | `{}` |
| `account` | `{}` | `{user, premium, expires?}` |

Times are RFC3339. File sizes are bytes. `added` must be true only when this
request created the provider torrent. The host selects the movie or episode
from `files`; it never sends executable selection callbacks to a plugin.
Unready acquisitions become cache misses. Cleanup only applies to newly added
torrents when the caller's removal policy permits it. A cached-only service may
return HTTP 501 for `find` and `remove`.

HTTP 401/403 means invalid credentials, 404/410 gone, 409 not cached, 429 rate
limited, and 501 unsupported. Other failures use a generic provider error.
Plugin links must be public HTTP(S) URLs; both link validation and every network
dial/redirect use the guarded transport. Native retry, cache, limiter and file
selection behavior applies. Plugin providers currently run after configured
built-in providers at priority 1000; source-card display order does not change
that priority.

Provide `/ether/health` with `status: "attention"` and a useful `reason` when
credentials are absent. `/ether/test` should verify the account and return
`{ok, message}` without exposing credentials or signed URLs. Offline installation
checks cannot establish that a paid account works; test it after setup.


## Source: docs/plugin-kinds.md

# Plugin content kinds

A content plugin adds a whole **library** to Ether — audiobooks,
comics, music, books, photos, field recordings, anything flat or
hierarchical — with no core changes. The owner meets each kind you
declare as a library beside Movies and TV Shows, in the console and
in every client app you publish it to.

This page is the contract. The worked example is
[`sdk/examples/kind-library`](../sdk/examples/kind-library); the
Studio "A new library" template generates the same skeleton from a
description.

## Declare a kind

In the manifest's `ether` block: `kind: "content"`, at least one of
the `catalog_provider` / `kind_resolver` capabilities (plus optional
`matcher` and `frontend_adapter`), and one entry per kind in
`contributes.mediaKinds`:

```jsonc
{
  "key": "recordings",              // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$, unique in the plugin
  "label": "Field recordings",
  "library": { "name": "Field Recordings" },   // default name; the owner can rename
  "levels": [                       // 1–5 levels, first is the root
    { "key": "collection", "label": "Collection" },
    { "key": "album", "label": "Album", "container": true },
    { "key": "track", "label": "Track", "playable": true }
  ],
  "fields": [                       // validated per item; indexed ones can facet
    { "key": "genre", "type": "string", "label": "Genre", "indexed": true },
    { "key": "durationSec", "type": "duration", "label": "Duration" }
  ],
  "present": { /* see "Publishing" */ },
  "browse": { "sorts": ["title", "index"], "facets": ["genre"], "search": true, "liveSearch": true },
  "sync": { "mode": "pull", "refresh": "1h" },
  "cache": { "maxBytes": 2147483648 },        // optional; per-library blob cache
  "match": { "thresholdDefault": 0.8 }        // optional
}
```

Rules that will bite if ignored: at least one level must be
`playable`; facet fields must be `indexed`; field keys may not reuse
envelope names (`id`, `title`, …); declarations are **additive across
versions** — removing or retyping a field/level is refused at upgrade
unless the owner agrees to replace the library's contents.

## The item envelope

Your provider returns `KindItem`s: your own `id` (letters, digits,
`. _ ~ -`, ≤128 chars — Ether namespaces it, you never see the stored
identity), `level`, `parentId`, `index` within the parent, `title`,
optional `summary/year/released/rating`, `playable`, counts, `art`
(`poster/backdrop/thumb/logo` plus declared roles), `fields` (checked
against your declaration; unknown keys are dropped, wrong types
reject the item), `hints` (an opaque JSON object ≤16 KiB, stored and
handed back to your resolver verbatim — put ids and locators there,
never secrets), and an `etag` for cheap re-syncs.

Caps: title 500 characters, summary 20k, each field 4k, 16 art roles.

## Routes Ether calls

Kind and setup routes are `GET`/`POST` with JSON in and out, through the
normal plugin transport. Frontend-adapter traffic keeps whatever method and
query the client sent:

| Route | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/browse` | Pull sync walks your catalogue | One level per call (`parentId`, `level`, `cursor`, `limit`). Return `nextCursor` or the full set up to `limit`; never more than `limit` items. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/changes` | Pull sync refresh | Optional delta feed `{upserts, deletes, nextCursor, complete}`. Answer 404/501 and Ether re-walks and diffs by `etag` instead. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/items/{id}` | Conformance and detail refresh | One full item. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/search` | Client searches, only when `browse.liveSearch` is on | Same page shape as browse with `query` set. Short budget; see below. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/resolve` | A viewer presses play | `{libraryKey, item, partIndex?, client?}` → ordered `sources`. Never called during browse. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/match` | Resolve-time matching, console re-match | `{item, candidates}` → `{matches:[{candidateRef, score 0..1, reasons}]}` best first. |
| `/ether/v1/setup/{step}/test` | The setup wizard | `{step, fields}` → `{ok, detail, fields?}`. Secrets arrive via `SecretGet`, never in this body. |
| `/ether/v1/frontend/{key}/…` | Your frontend adapter's traffic | Any method, and the original query string (repeated keys flatten to the first value). Ether authenticated the viewer first; you get `X-Ether-Viewer` headers, never a credential. |

Clients are **always served from Ether's store** — browse, search
and detail never call you live, so nothing scales with your catalogue
size. You are called at sync time and at play time.

Sync modes: **pull** (Ether walks `browse`, then polls `changes` on
your `refresh`, minimum 15m) or **push** (you call the `KindUpsert`
host service; refused for pull kinds — one writer per kind). A pull
walk that would delete more than half the library aborts and raises
owner attention instead of wiping it.

### Live search

With `browse.liveSearch: true`, a client search on your library also
calls your `/search` route with a short budget (about two seconds).
Results are validated, **upserted into the store like synced items**
(stubs are fine — playable leaves resolve at play time), and merged
with local results. On timeout or error the viewer gets local
results in time and your late answer still lands in the store for
the next search. Declare it only if your source can answer a search
quickly; the Studio template has it on with the explanation beside
the toggle. Pair it with `browse.search: true` so earlier live
results stay findable locally.

## Resolving bytes

`resolve` returns ordered `PlayableSource`s; Ether tries them in
order. Patterns:

- **file** — a hosted resolver path inside an owner-picked folder; requires
  `folders: read` and live containment checks when resolving and opening.
- **range** — a URL Ether reads with HTTP Range (demoted to download
  when the host cannot range and the size fits the cache).
- **download** — fetched whole into the per-library blob cache
  (SHA-256 checked when you provide one), then served locally.
- **direct** — the client surface is handed the URL (only where the
  surface supports it).
- **container** — one member of a zip/RAR/7z, possibly multi-volume:
  `{volumes:[{url,size}], member}` or `memberIndex`. Passwords come
  from a named settings secret (`passwordSecret`), never from your
  response. Ether caches the extracted member.
- **release** — hand Ether a magnet/infohash/NZB and its existing
  debrid/Usenet/torrent pipeline opens it. For torrents, set
  `release.fileIndex` (zero-based index in the provider's complete file list),
  `release.candidate.fileIndex`, or `release.file` (exact path or unique
  basename) to open audio, books, comics, ROMs or other non-video files.
  A top-level `fileIndex` overrides the candidate's index. If both index and
  `file` are supplied they must identify the same file. Empty files,
  invalid indices and missing or ambiguous names fail without fallback.
  Without either selector the existing video picker is used. In Go, indices
  are `*int`: a pointer to zero selects the first file; nil leaves selection
  automatic. Indices refer to the provider's ordering, not its file IDs;
  prefer a path when the provider's ordering is unknown. Explicit selectors
  on an NZB release are rejected; use a container source for archive members.
  `fileHint` retains its existing meaning as an archive member hint.

`ResolveSources({kind: "indexer_search", query, category})` accepts a
comma-separated list of Newznab category IDs (`"3000"`, `"7030"`) or standard
names: `console`, `movies`/`movie`, `audio`/`music`, `pc`, `tv`, `adult`,
`books`, `comics`, `other`. It sends a generic search with those categories
and the query unchanged, rather than assuming a movie or TV request.
Invalid categories are rejected. Stremio/addon sources do not support this
filter and reject scoped searches. Omit `category` for the default media
search. Results and acquired files are cached separately by category and
file selection. The wire shapes are documented in
[`plugin-sources.v1.json`](../schemas/plugin-sources.v1.json).

URLs may carry `{itemIndex}`, `{pageNumber}` (= itemIndex + 1),
`{byteStart}`, `{byteEnd}` and `{byteRange}` placeholders; Ether
substitutes integers only. Resolver `headers` may use
`{secret:name}` placeholders, substituted host-side — never put a
raw secret in a response (responses are logged). Returning zero
sources means "not available right now" and is cached briefly.

With `permissions.sources: "search"` (or `"acquire"` to open debrid
content) your resolver can ask Ether to find bytes through the
owner's indexers and debrid via the `ResolveSources` host service,
rank the candidates yourself (or in `/match`), and return a
`release` source.

Watch state and progress are keyed per playable leaf. For paged
media, store progress against the leaf the viewer is on (its index
is the natural unit); containers themselves carry no progress.

## Publishing (`present`)

Each library publishes per protocol; the owner can override your
defaults per library afterwards.

- `plex: {base: "movie"|"show"|"artist"|"photo"}` — root→show/artist,
  middle→season/album, leaf→episode/track. More than three levels
  are flattened with indexes kept (the Studio preview shows this).
- `mediaBrowser: {collectionType, itemTypes}` — Jellyfin/Emby.
  Item types: `Movie, Series, Season, Episode, MusicAlbum, Audio,
  Book, PhotoAlbum, Photo`, mapped per level; unmapped levels use
  the collection's natural container.
- `stremio: {type}`, `xtream: {category}`, `silo: {type}`.
- `adapterOnly: true` — no generic mapping fits; ship a
  `frontend_adapter` and serve the protocol yourself. Embed
  `/ether/v1/kind-media/{itemId}` stream URLs for bytes (the SDKs'
  `StreamURL`/`stream_url`/`streamUrl` helper) instead of proxying
  media through the adapter.

A library the owner cannot see is invisible to that viewer on every
surface; you never check viewer permissions yourself.

## Matching

Matching is yours; persistence and the console are Ether's. A manual
pin from the item drawer always wins, then your best score at or
above the kind's threshold (manifest default, owner-editable), then
an inline match during resolve. Give plain-language `reasons` — the
owner reads them.

## Host services

Beyond the usual services, kind plugins get (capability-checked on
every call): `KindUpsert` / `KindDelete` (push kinds), `KindItems`
(read your own library back), `ResolveSources`, and
`CachePut` / `CacheOpen` for the per-library blob cache
(content-addressed `blob:<sha256>` refs; you never name paths).
Default cache quota is 2 GiB per library under a shared cap of
min(10 GiB, 5% of the cache disk); your `cache.maxBytes` and the
owner can override it.

## Setup

Declare `contributes.setup.steps` (any plugin kind): each step lists
settings fields and an optional test route. The console walks the
steps in a drawer; a content plugin's libraries stay hidden and sync
waits until required steps pass (the owner may skip, and sees a
setup banner instead).

## SDKs

Same contract in all three, pinned by the shared fixtures in
`sdk/conformance/kinds` (each SDK's tests replay them):

- **Go** (`sdk/go`): `Plugin.OnCatalog / OnResolve / OnMatch /
  OnFrontend / OnSetupTest`, the `CatalogProvider`, `KindResolver`,
  `KindMatcher`, `FrontendAdapter` interfaces, host kind methods on
  `Host`, and `sdk/go/kit` helpers — `scrape` (polite host-HTTP
  fetching), `archivex` (zip/cbz/epub members), `metaparse` (EPUB
  OPF, ComicInfo, ID3, FLAC), `feedparse` (RSS/Atom/JSON Feed →
  items), `hints` (typed hints/fields).
- **Python** (`sdk/python`): `CatalogProvider`, `KindResolver`,
  `KindMatcher`, `FrontendAdapter`, `SetupTester` base classes with
  `on_catalog` etc., `ctx.ether.kinds` / `.cache`, `parse_feed` and
  `archive_list` helpers.
- **TypeScript** (`sdk/typescript`): `onCatalog / onResolve /
  onMatch / onFrontend / onSetupTest`, `ctx.ether.kinds` / `.cache`,
  `parseFeed`, `archiveList`, `scrapeText/Links`.

Content plugins are usually best as `remote` (scraping wants a real
process); `hosted` works for pure-API providers — the example and
the Studio template are hosted. In hosted JS, read settings with
`ether.settings.get()` and kind services via `ether.kinds`,
`ether.sources`, `ether.cache`.

## Checking your work

- The conformance kit (`kit.CheckKindProvider`, run by Studio and
  `ether plugin check`) walks your provider offline: pagination must
  terminate, pages must fit the limit, detail must round-trip, a
  declared live search must answer, resolver sources must use known
  patterns and placeholders.
- Studio's kind preview browses your draft, shows the hierarchy and
  the per-protocol projection, and dry-runs the resolver on a real
  leaf (template expansion included) before anything is installed.
- Start from the Studio "A new library" template or copy
  `sdk/examples/kind-library`; its test is the executable version of
  this page.


### Granted local files (hosted runtime)

A resolver can return a source such as
`{"id":"local","pattern":"file","path":"/picked/library/Game.nds","mime":"application/octet-stream"}`.
This requires `folders: read` and an owner-picked, non-revoked folder grant.
Ether uses the same `validateLocalFile` and `openGrantedLocalFile` path as
Stremio `ether.file`: it rejects `..`, resolves symlinks, checks containment at
resolve time and again at open time, and opens through `os.OpenRoot`.
Remote/sidecar resolvers cannot serve host files with this pattern.

### File identification without file contents

Hosted plugins can call `ether.folders.hash(root, path)` (TypeScript SDK:
`host.folders.hash`; Go SDK: `FoldersHash`). `path` is relative to the picked
root. The service requires `folders: read` and the same live folder grant as
`folders.stat`. It refuses traversal, symlink escapes and non-regular files.
It returns `{size, modTime, crc32, md5, sha1}`: Unix seconds for `modTime`,
lowercase hexadecimal digests (CRC32 IEEE, 8 digits; MD5, 32; SHA1, 40).
No file contents cross the plugin boundary. All three hashes are computed in
one streaming pass with fixed memory. `hash` stays synchronous for files up to
256 MiB; larger files must use `hashStart(root, path)` (Go: `FoldersHashStart`).
This explicitly starts a background job and returns `{id, state, bytes}`.
Poll `hashPoll(id)` (`FoldersHashPoll`) for bytes processed and state: `running`,
`done`, `canceled`, or `error`. A done job includes `result` with the hash object;
an error includes `error`. `hashCancel(id)` (`FoldersHashCancel`) requests cancellation;
poll until terminal to observe completion. Start and poll do not return file bytes.

There is no file-size ceiling for jobs. At most one runs per plugin and two
across the process; a busy start returns an error to retry later. Starting the
same active root/path returns its existing job ID. Readers yield for 2 ms after
each 1 MiB chunk. Jobs survive the initiating call, have a 24-hour deadline,
and recheck grants and cancellation every chunk. Files changing during hashing
abort without caching. Revocation or plugin disable stops ongoing reads.

Successful digests persist in a host-owned database cache indexed by plugin,
resolved path, size and nanosecond modification time. Unchanged files reuse the
cached digest after permission and containment checks. Cache rows are removed
when the plugin is uninstalled. Only explicitly requested files are hashed.
Job status is process-local, and each plugin's terminal status is retained until
its next start; after a restart, start again to reuse any completed cached result.
SDK sidecars cannot use these hosted folder services.

### Item availability

An upsert can carry
`"unavailable":{"code":"no_verified_source","detail":"No source matched the DAT record"}`.
The code must be nonempty and at most 128 bytes; detail is optional and at most
2000 bytes. The item remains visible in browse/counts so owners can inspect the
coverage gap. Ether exposes the reason in the item drawer, marks the item
nonplayable, and never calls its resolver or opens a cached resolution while
this declaration is present. The declaration also travels in frontend item
details. The next upsert without `unavailable` clears it, even with the same
etag. This is independent of the level's `playable` capability; clearing the
reason does not grant playback to a nonplayable level.

### Large downloads and ZIP members (v0.3.11)

Hosted and remote clients can keep large data in the host's existing library
blob cache, without copying the complete file into guest memory:

```ts
const cached = await ctx.ether.http.fetchToCache!({
  url: "https://datasets.example/platform.zip",
  libraryKey: "pk-community-example-library-games", // this plugin's own library
  name: "platform.zip",
});
const members = await ctx.ether.archive!.list(cached.blob);
const member = members.find(m => m.name === "games/example.json")!;
const chunk = await ctx.ether.archive!.open(cached.blob, member.index, {
  offset: 0, length: Math.min(member.size, 1048576),
}); // Uint8Array; request another range for the next piece
```

`http.fetchToCache({url, headers?, libraryKey, name})` performs a GET, streams
up to the owner download ceiling (8 GiB by default), further bounded by the library cache quota, into the plugin's own library cache, and returns
`{blob, size, crc32, md5, sha1, status}`. SHA-256 is the blob reference.
Digests cover the stored response bytes in one pass. Compare the digest with
trusted catalogue metadata before serving a verified download. Non-2xx responses,
network failures, size overflow and quota failures return errors; they do not
publish a truncated blob. Redirects recheck the live network grant and the
existing SSRF policy. The existing content capability, network host declaration
and library cache quota apply; no new permission is needed. The operation is
synchronous and bounded by the current call's deadline; there is no background
prefetch. Cache eviction still applies to returned refs.

`cache.read(blob, {offset, length})` reads at most 1 MiB from a cached blob.
`archive.list(blob)` returns `[{index, name, size}]`, reading the ZIP directory
without loading all compressed bytes. `archive.open(blob, memberIndex,
{offset, length})` returns at most 1 MiB from the **uncompressed** member.
Offsets are nonnegative integers; lengths are 1..1048576. A read at EOF returns
empty bytes and reads crossing EOF return the available suffix. Raw host calls
return `{bodyBase64, size}`; SDK clients decode this into bytes. Every call opens
only the calling plugin's cache namespace and closes the reader afterward.
The Go `RemoteHostClient` provides `FetchToCache`, `CacheRead`, `ArchiveList` and
`ArchiveOpen` through the optional `BlobHost` interface, with `DataRange` options.

ZIP sizes and member counts use owner global/per-plugin ceilings: defaults are
8 GiB compressed archive/member, 32 GiB total expansion and 65,535 members.
The central directory is bounded to 64 MiB (1024 bytes per member name), with a
1000:1 maximum expansion ratio per member. ZIP64 is supported; split archives
remain unsupported. Store and Deflate are supported. Unsafe paths, special files, encryption,
Split archives are rejected. Nothing is extracted to a filesystem.
Deflate ranges inflate and discard up to the requested offset on each call;
prefer large sequential chunks, and avoid repeatedly rescanning a large member.
Range reads do not independently verify the full member CRC; use trusted digests
when integrity matters. Local owner-granted paths are not archive inputs: first
use a plugin-owned cached blob. Gzip files are not ZIPs and are unsupported here.
An HTTP `Content-Encoding: gzip` response may be transparently decoded by the
HTTP client; its digests then describe the decoded bytes. A `.gz` file is not
automatically decompressed by this archive service.

Direct `http.fetch` still limits the raw response to 10 MiB. Its JSON result
allowance now includes encoding expansion (binary base64 or escaped text), so the
4 MiB general host-result cap no longer blocks that documented limit. This is
an I/O ceiling, not a guarantee of guest heap space: the default guest has 32 MiB
and the owner ceiling defaults to 2 GiB (adjustable up to wasm32 4 GiB), with temporary JSON strings and parsed objects
using additional memory. Use fetch-to-cache and ranged reads for large inputs;
do not concatenate all chunks into one guest buffer. Other host results remain
capped at 4 MiB.

### Owner-started multi-call work and resource requests

A page action returning `{job: "build-catalogue"}` starts a background job.
The job returns `continueInMs`, an opaque JSON `continuation`, and a `progress`
string to continue; Ether forwards the token in the next POST body. `done: true`
finishes, `failed: "reason"` fails, and an absent `continueInMs` finishes too.
Jobs use the owner's time ceiling (12h by default), a 1,000,000-call sanity bound,
a minimum 100ms pause, OS background CPU/IO priority, and cooperative pauses
between calls and host operations during playback, Live TV or high host load.
They are cancellable with visible progress. Persist checkpoints in KV for
recovery on a later owner action after restart; Ether does not resume eagerly.

`ether.runtime.limits` requests memory, time, compute, download and archive
resources within owner-controlled global/per-plugin ceilings. Defaults: 2 GiB
memory ceiling (up to 4 GiB; omitted heap request stays 32 MiB), 12h, effectively
unlimited background work units, 8 GiB download/member, 32 GiB total expansion,
and 65,535 members. The library cache quota further bounds downloads. The owner
sees requested versus granted values before install and in the drawer, and can
raise or lower ceilings under Plugins → Settings or for one plugin. Saving
stops affected jobs so the new ceilings apply immediately.

Viewer browse/search/playback calls retain tight budgets: `/stream/`, `/catalog/`,
`/meta/`, `/subtitles/`, `/ether/open`, `/ether/metadata/`, `/ether/subtitles/`,
`/ether/markers`, and `/ether/v1/kinds/` use at most 10,000 units/30s plus tighter
route/caller deadlines. Ranking budgets stay unchanged. Administrative setup,
actions, tools, events and jobs use owner grants. Health/configuration/view/options
keep short protocol deadlines. See the SDK README for exact fields and APIs.

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ValidExternalID

``````
// ValidExternalID reports whether id is a legal plugin external id
// (spec §2.2: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._~-]{0,127}$, no ':' or '/').
func ValidExternalID(id string) bool {
	if len(id) == 0 || len(id) > 128 {
		return false
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(id); i++ {
		c := id[i]
		alnum := (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
		if i == 0 {
			if !alnum {
				return false
			}
			continue
		}
		if !alnum && c != '.' && c != '_' && c != '~' && c != '-' {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ItemRef.Parse

``````
// Parse splits r into (pluginID, kindKey, externalID) and reports
// whether r is a well-formed ItemRef (spec §2.2).
func (r ItemRef) Parse() (pluginID, kindKey, externalID string, ok bool) {
	s, hasPrefix := strings.CutPrefix(string(r), "pk:")
	if !hasPrefix {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	p1 := strings.IndexByte(s, ':')
	if p1 <= 0 {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	pluginID = s[:p1]
	rest := s[p1+1:]
	p2 := strings.IndexByte(rest, ':')
	if p2 <= 0 {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	kindKey = rest[:p2]
	externalID = rest[p2+1:]
	if strings.ContainsRune(pluginID, '/') || strings.ContainsRune(kindKey, '/') || !ValidExternalID(externalID) {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	return pluginID, kindKey, externalID, true
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ParseItemRef

``````
// ParseItemRef validates s and returns it as an ItemRef.
func ParseItemRef(s string) (ItemRef, error) {
	ref := ItemRef(s)
	if _, _, _, ok := ref.Parse(); !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("itemRef %q: invalid format", s)
	}
	return ref, nil
}
``````

``````
// Valid reports whether r is a well-formed ItemRef.
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#PluginLibraryKey

``````
// PluginLibraryKey is the library key a plugin kind owns
// (spec §1.1): "pk-" + slug(pluginID) + "-" + slug(kindKey), matching
// internal/libraries.UpsertPluginLibrary. The key is an opaque unique
// slug; ownership is always read back from the stored plugin/kind
// columns, never parsed out of the key.
func PluginLibraryKey(pluginID, kindKey string) string {
	return "pk-" + libraryKeySlug(pluginID) + "-" + libraryKeySlug(kindKey)
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#libraryKeySlug

``````
func libraryKeySlug(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	dash := false
	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)) {
		switch {
		case unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r):
			if dash && b.Len() > 0 {
				b.WriteByte('-')
			}
			dash = false
			b.WriteRune(r)
		default:
			dash = true
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}
``````

``````
	j.status.State, j.status.Error = state, reason
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.startActionJob

``````
// startActionJob runs only owner-started work. At most two jobs run per plugin;
// at most sixteen route snapshots are retained per plugin, including running jobs.
func (m *Manager) startActionJob(pluginID string, body json.RawMessage) error {
	var out struct {
		Job string `json:"job"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &out) != nil || out.Job == "" {
		return nil
	}
	path := out.Job
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "/ether/job/") {
		path = "/ether/job/" + strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/")
	}
	if len(path) > 256 || strings.Contains(path, "..") || strings.ContainsAny(path, "?#\\") {
		return nil
	}
	key := pluginID + "|" + path
	m.jobsMu.Lock()
	defer m.jobsMu.Unlock()
	if old, ok := m.jobs.Load(key); ok && old.(*actionJob).snapshot().State == "running" {
		return nil
	}
	active, count := 0, 0
	oldestKey := ""
	var oldest time.Time
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(k.(string), pluginID+"|") {
			return true
		}
		s := v.(*actionJob).snapshot()
		count++
		if s.State == "running" {
			active++
		} else if oldestKey == "" || s.Started.Before(oldest) {
			oldestKey, oldest = k.(string), s.Started
		}
		return true
	})
	if active >= 2 {
		return fmt.Errorf("two background jobs are already running; wait for one to finish")
	}
	if _, exists := m.jobs.Load(key); !exists && count >= 16 {
		m.jobs.Delete(oldestKey)
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline)
	j := &actionJob{cancel: cancel, status: ActionJobStatus{Path: path, State: "running", Started: time.Now().UTC(), TotalLimitMS: m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline.Milliseconds(), AttemptLimit: ActionJobAttempts}}
	m.jobs.Store(key, j)
	go func() {
		runtime.LockOSThread() // Do not unlock: this lowered-priority thread is discarded on return.
		lowerJobPriority()
		defer cancel()
		err := runActionJob(ctx, j, ActionJobAttempts, func(ctx context.Context, token json.RawMessage) (Response, error) {
			if err := wasm.WaitBackground(ctx, m.deps.Busy); err != nil {
				return Response{}, err
			}
			payload, _ := json.Marshal(struct {
				Continuation json.RawMessage `json:"continuation,omitempty"`
			}{token})
			return m.Call(ctx, pluginID, Request{Method: "POST", Path: path, Body: payload})
		})
		if err != nil {
			state := "error"
			if ctx.Err() == context.Canceled {
				state = "canceled"
			}
			if ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded {
				err = fmt.Errorf("job reached its total time limit of %s", m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline)
			}
			reason := m.store.redactKnown(context.Background(), pluginID, err.Error())
			j.finish(state, reason)
			m.log.Warn("plugins: action job", "plugin", pluginID, "job", path, "err", reason)
		} else {
			j.finish("done", "")
		}
	}()
	return nil
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#runActionJob

``````
// runActionJob treats an absent continuation flag as completion for existing
// one-call jobs. Explicit failures and non-success HTTP responses always stop.
func runActionJob(ctx context.Context, j *actionJob, attempts int, call func(context.Context, json.RawMessage) (Response, error)) error {
	var token json.RawMessage
	for n := 0; n < attempts; n++ {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("job stopped: %w", err)
		}
		j.mu.Lock()
		j.status.Attempts++
		j.mu.Unlock()
		resp, err := call(ctx, token)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("job stopped: %w", err)
		}
		if resp.Status < 200 || resp.Status >= 300 {
			return fmt.Errorf("job returned HTTP %d", resp.Status)
		}
		var step struct {
			ContinueInMS *int64          `json:"continueInMs"`
			Continuation json.RawMessage `json:"continuation"`
			Progress     string          `json:"progress"`
			Done         bool            `json:"done"`
			Failed       string          `json:"failed"`
		}
		if len(resp.Body) > 0 {
			if err = json.Unmarshal(resp.Body, &step); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("invalid job response: %w", err)
			}
		}
		if len(step.Progress) > 1024 {
			return fmt.Errorf("job progress exceeds 1024 bytes")
		}
		j.mu.Lock()
		if step.Progress != "" {
			j.status.Progress = step.Progress
		}
		j.mu.Unlock()
		if step.Failed != "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("job failed: %.1024s", step.Failed)
		}
		if step.Done || step.ContinueInMS == nil {
			return nil
		}
		if *step.ContinueInMS < 0 || *step.ContinueInMS > 300000 {
			return fmt.Errorf("continueInMs must be between 0 and 300000")
		}
		if len(step.Continuation) > 64<<10 {
			return fmt.Errorf("job continuation exceeds 64 KiB")
		}
		token = step.Continuation
		if n+1 == attempts {
			break
		}
		timer := time.NewTimer(max(actionJobMinDelay, time.Duration(*step.ContinueInMS)*time.Millisecond))
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			timer.Stop()
			return fmt.Errorf("job stopped: %w", ctx.Err())
		case <-timer.C:
		}
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("job reached its limit of %d calls", attempts)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.cancelActionJobs

``````
func (m *Manager) cancelActionJobs(id string) {
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		if id == "" || strings.HasPrefix(k.(string), id+"|") {
			v.(*actionJob).cancel()
		}
		return true
	})
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.handleActionJobs

``````
func (m *Manager) handleActionJobs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.PathValue("id")
	if _, err := m.Get(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
		m.fail(w, err)
		return
	}
	jobs := []ActionJobStatus{}
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		if strings.HasPrefix(k.(string), id+"|") {
			s := v.(*actionJob).snapshot()
			s.Progress = m.store.redactKnown(r.Context(), id, s.Progress)
			jobs = append(jobs, s)
		}
		return true
	})
	sort.Slice(jobs, func(i, j int) bool { return jobs[i].Started.After(jobs[j].Started) })
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, jobs)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.handleCancelActionJob

``````
func (m *Manager) handleCancelActionJob(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req struct {
		Path string `json:"path"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid", "The request was not understood.", nil)
		return
	}
	if job, ok := m.jobs.Load(r.PathValue("id") + "|" + req.Path); ok {
		job.(*actionJob).cancel()
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]bool{"ok": true})
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#Manifest

``````
// Manifest is a plugin's manifest.json: the Stremio manifest fields, typed
// by the one Stremio model (internal/stremio), plus Ether's fields under
// Ether (SPEC §5.1.1). A manifest with a nil Ether is a plain Stremio
// add-on. Every Stremio rule (resources, ids, catalogs, extras) is the
// library's, reached through Stremio().
type Manifest struct {
	ID            string                `json:"id"`
	Version       string                `json:"version"`
	Name          string                `json:"name"`
	Description   string                `json:"description,omitempty"`
	Logo          string                `json:"logo,omitempty"`
	Background    string                `json:"background,omitempty"`
	Types         []string              `json:"types,omitempty"`
	AddonCatalogs []StremioCat          `json:"addonCatalogs,omitempty"`
	Catalogs      []StremioCat          `json:"catalogs,omitempty"`
	Resources     stremio.Resources     `json:"resources,omitempty"`
	IDPrefixes    []string              `json:"idPrefixes,omitempty"`
	BehaviorHints stremio.BehaviorHints `json:"behaviorHints,omitzero"`
	Ether         *EtherBlock           `json:"ether,omitempty"`
	// rolesOff are capabilities the owner switched off on the installed
	// record (Record.RolesOff); EffectiveEther leaves them out.
	rolesOff []Capability
}
``````

``````
// Stremio is the manifest's Stremio part.

	return stremio.Manifest{
		ID: m.ID, Version: m.Version, Name: m.Name, Description: m.Description, Logo: m.Logo,
		Background: m.Background, Types: m.Types, IDPrefixes: m.IDPrefixes, Resources: m.Resources,
		Catalogs: m.Catalogs, AddonCatalogs: m.AddonCatalogs, BehaviorHints: m.BehaviorHints,
	}
}
``````

``````
// EtherBlock is the `ether` object of a manifest.
type EtherBlock struct {
	Protocol int `json:"protocol"`
	// Stremio marks a native plugin that answers Stremio add-on routes,
	// such as an add-on opened and edited in Studio: Ether talks to it
	// exactly as to the add-on it came from.
	Stremio      bool         `json:"stremio,omitempty"`
	Kind         Kind         `json:"kind"`
	Capabilities []Capability `json:"capabilities,omitempty"`
	// Summary is plain text or a "$t:key" reference into Strings.
	Summary string      `json:"summary,omitempty"`
	Author  Author      `json:"author,omitempty"`
	License string      `json:"license,omitempty"`
	Repo    string      `json:"repo,omitempty"`
	Icon    string      `json:"icon,omitempty"`
	Runtime RuntimeDecl `json:"runtime"`
	// Sidecar tells the console how to run a remote plugin's program: a
	// Docker image, a download+command pair, or neither (docs only). Only
	// meaningful when Runtime.Kind is "remote".
	Sidecar *SidecarDecl `json:"sidecar,omitempty"`
	// Cluster is "leader" (default) or "every_node".
	Cluster     string      `json:"cluster,omitempty"`
	Health      HealthDecl  `json:"health,omitempty"`
	Permissions Permissions `json:"permissions,omitempty"`
	// Settings is a settings schema (SPEC §5.5), {} or {"$ref":"file"}.
	Settings json.RawMessage `json:"settings,omitempty"`
	// Strings maps a locale to a file path (string) or an inline
	// key-to-text object. "en" is required when any $t: key is used.
	Strings     map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"strings,omitempty"`
	Schedule    []ScheduleEntry            `json:"schedule,omitempty"`
	Contributes Contributes                `json:"contributes,omitempty"`
}
``````

``````
// RuntimeKind is the runtime that serves the plugin. A plain Stremio
// add-on (no ether block) is always reached over HTTP: "remote".
func (m Manifest) RuntimeKind() string {
	if m.Ether == nil || m.Ether.Runtime.Kind == "" {
		return "remote"
	}
	return m.Ether.Runtime.Kind
}
``````

``````
	Commands       []CommandMeta       `json:"commands,omitempty"`
	// MediaKinds declares the content kinds this plugin serves; each entry
	// that declares a library block becomes its own library (spec §2.1).
	MediaKinds []MediaKindMeta `json:"mediaKinds,omitempty"`
	// FrontendAdapters declares protocol surfaces this plugin serves
	// through Ether's generic adapter frontend (spec §6.5).
	FrontendAdapters []FrontendAdapterMeta `json:"frontendAdapters,omitempty"`
	// Setup declares guided setup steps for any plugin kind (§8).
	Setup *SetupMeta `json:"setup,omitempty"`
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#DefaultKindCacheMaxBytes

``````
// Blob cache budget defaults (§15.5): the per-library default quota and
// the shared absolute cap. The shared cap is also bounded by 5% of the
// cache disk at runtime, which only the cache owner can measure.
const (
	DefaultKindCacheMaxBytes int64 = 2 << 30
	SharedKindCacheCapBytes  int64 = 10 << 30
)
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#KindCacheDecl.EffectiveMaxBytes

``````
// EffectiveMaxBytes resolves the declared cache cap against the default.
func (c KindCacheDecl) EffectiveMaxBytes() int64 {
	if c.MaxBytes <= 0 {
		return DefaultKindCacheMaxBytes
	}
	return c.MaxBytes
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#Runtime

``````
// Runtime is how the host reaches one installed plugin. WS8a (hosted) and
// WS8b (remote) implement it; tests use a fake. Call must honour ctx
// deadlines. Close releases the instance; the host may open a fresh one
// after a failure (restart with backoff).
type Runtime interface {
	Call(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Response, error)
	Close() error
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#Host

``````
// Host is the set of Ether services a plugin may call (SPEC §5.1.5).
// Every method re-checks the plugin's live grants, so a revoke takes
// effect mid-call. Writes are journalled; in shadow mode they are
// recorded without applying. The hosted runtime exposes Host as imports;
// remote plugins reach it over /ether/plugin-host/* (WS8b).
type Host interface {
	KVGet(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]byte, bool, error)
	KVPut(ctx context.Context, key string, value []byte) error
	KVDelete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
	KVList(ctx context.Context, prefix string) ([]string, error)

	// SecretGet returns a sealed setting the manifest declared in
	// permissions.secrets. Hosted plugins only.
	SecretGet(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error)

	// HTTPFetch fetches through egress and safefetch; only manifest
	// network hosts are allowed. Observed hosts feed the privacy label.
	HTTPFetch(ctx context.Context, req FetchRequest) (FetchResponse, error)

	// CatalogSearch and CatalogGet need catalog: read. Results are JSON
	// title summaries produced by the injected catalog backend.
	CatalogSearch(ctx context.Context, query string, limit, offset int) (json.RawMessage, error)
	CatalogGet(ctx context.Context, id string) (json.RawMessage, error)

	// ViewerHistory needs viewers.watch_history for that viewer.
	ViewerGranted(ctx context.Context) (json.RawMessage, error)
	ViewerHistory(ctx context.Context, viewerID int64, limit, offset int) (json.RawMessage, error)
	// SetWatchState needs viewers.write_watch_state; journalled.
	SetWatchState(ctx context.Context, viewerID int64, titleID string, watched bool) error
	// CollectionsUpsert needs collections: write; journalled.
	CollectionsUpsert(ctx context.Context, collection json.RawMessage) error

	// KindUpsert and KindDelete need catalog_provider and a push-mode
	// kind (spec §3.6): the sync engine is the only writer for pull
	// kinds. Writes are journalled in shadow mode without applying.
	KindUpsert(ctx context.Context, kindKey string, items []core.KindItem) (accepted int, err error)
	KindDelete(ctx context.Context, kindKey string, externalIDs []string) error
	// KindItems reads the plugin's own library back, keyset-paged.
	KindItems(ctx context.Context, kindKey, cursor string, limit int) (core.KindPage, error)
	// ResolveSources needs kind_resolver and permissions.sources
	// (search to look, acquire to open debrid content, §4.5).
	ResolveSources(ctx context.Context, q core.SourceQuery) ([]core.SourceCandidate, error)
	// CachePut stores one blob in a kind library's cache namespace and
	// returns its "blob:<sha256>" reference; CacheOpen reads one back.
	CachePut(ctx context.Context, libraryKey, name string, r io.Reader) (blobRef string, err error)
	CacheOpen(ctx context.Context, blobRef string) (io.ReadSeekCloser, error)

	// StreamURL mints a short-lived, scoped ticket for one of this
	// plugin's own kind items and returns the Ether stream URL a frontend
	// adapter embeds instead of a plugin URL (spec §6.5). The viewer is
	// the one the proxied request authenticated (X-Ether-Viewer); items
	// from another plugin, or a library the viewer cannot see, are
	// refused. Bytes are then served by Ether, never by the plugin.
	StreamURL(ctx context.Context, itemRef string) (string, error)

	// FoldersList and FoldersStat need folders: read and an owner-picked
	// root. They never return file contents.
	FoldersList(ctx context.Context, root, path string) ([]FolderEntry, error)
	FoldersStat(ctx context.Context, root, path string) (FolderEntry, error)
	FoldersHash(ctx context.Context, root, path string) (FolderHash, error)
	FoldersHashStart(ctx context.Context, root, path string) (FolderHashJob, error)
	FoldersHashPoll(ctx context.Context, id string) (FolderHashJob, error)
	FoldersHashCancel(ctx context.Context, id string) (FolderHashJob, error)

	// Settings returns the plugin's current non-secret settings. Plugins
	// read them per request instead of keeping them in instance memory,
	// because hosted plugins run in a pool of instances that restart.
	// Secrets stay behind SecretGet.
	Settings(ctx context.Context) (map[string]any, error)

	// NotifyOwner posts a console notice (rate-limited).
	NotifyOwner(ctx context.Context, text string) error
	// Log appends to the plugin's log ring (redacted, rate-limited).
	Log(ctx context.Context, level, msg string, attrs map[string]any) error
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#Catalogue

``````
// Catalogue is the signed catalogue hook used by the owner API, install
// and update flows (WS12).
type Catalogue interface {
	http.Handler
	// Resolve looks up a plugin in the verified catalogue by plugin ID (or
	// artifact URL) and optional version (empty means latest). It fails when
	// the plugin is not in the catalogue or is revoked.
	Resolve(ctx context.Context, idOrURL, version string) (CatalogueArtifact, error)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/contract.go#*ValidationError.Error

``````
func (e *ValidationError) Error() string {
	if len(e.Fields) == 0 {
		return "plugins: invalid"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("plugins: invalid: %s: %s", e.Fields[0].Field, e.Fields[0].Message)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/descriptors.go#textOf

``````
// textOf converts a manifest label ("$t:key" or plain text) to registry
// Text. Plain plugin text is carried as Resolved so the console shows it
// without a catalogue entry; $t: keys resolve through plugin strings.
func textOf(plugin, s string) extend.Text {
	if strings.HasPrefix(s, "$t:") {
		return extend.PluginText(plugin, strings.TrimPrefix(s, "$t:"))
	}
	return extend.Text{Resolved: s}
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/descriptors.go#DescriptorsFor

``````
// DescriptorsFor builds the registry descriptors a manifest contributes.
// Exported for the kit and Studio previews.
func DescriptorsFor(man Manifest) []extend.Descriptor {
	man.Ether = man.EffectiveEther()
	id := man.ID
	c := man.Ether.Contributes
	var out []extend.Descriptor
	add := func(kind extend.Kind, key string, label extend.Text, meta any) {
		d := extend.Descriptor{Kind: kind, ID: extend.PluginID(id, key), Owner: id, Label: label, Group: man.Name}
		if meta != nil {
			d = d.WithMeta(meta)
		}
		out = append(out, d)
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapOnAirContent) {
		for _, seg := range c.OnAirSegments {
			add(extend.KindOnAirSegment, seg.ID, textOf(id, seg.Name), map[string]any{"duration": seg.Duration, "rating": seg.Rating, "feeds": seg.Feeds})
		}
	}
	for _, p := range c.Pages {
		meta := map[string]any{"route": p.Route, "pluginRoute": "/api/plugins/" + id + "/views/" + p.Key, "icon": p.Icon}
		if p.Group != "" {
			meta["group"] = p.Group
		}
		add(extend.KindPage, p.Key, textOf(id, p.Label), meta)
		add(extend.KindNavItem, "page-"+p.Key, textOf(id, p.Label), map[string]any{
			"route": "/plugins/" + id + "/" + p.Key, "pageKey": p.Key})
	}
	for _, s := range c.Slots {
		add(extend.KindSlot, s.Key, textOf(id, s.Label), map[string]any{"slot": s.Slot, "route": s.Route, "action": s.Action, "key": s.Key})
	}
	for _, cm := range c.Commands {
		add(extend.KindCommand, cm.Key, textOf(id, cm.Label), map[string]any{"action": cm.Action})
	}
	for _, rs := range c.RankingSteps {
		add(extend.KindRankingStep, rs.Key, textOf(id, rs.Label), map[string]any{
			"editor": rs.Editor, "budget": rs.Budget, "hint": rs.Hint})
	}
	for _, rc := range c.RuleConditions {
		add(extend.KindRuleField, rc.Key, textOf(id, rc.Label), map[string]any{
			"operators": rc.Operators, "editor": rc.Editor})
	}
	for _, ls := range c.ListSources {
		if !man.HasCapability(CapListSource) {
			continue
		}
		pid := extend.PluginID(id, ls.Key)
		fields, defaults := ParamFieldsFromList(id, ParseListParamFields(ls.Params))
		var values map[string]any
		_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(defaults), &values)
		sourceDefaults := map[string]any{}
		if len(values) > 0 {
			sourceDefaults["params"] = values
		}
		meta := map[string]any{
			"catalog":          ls.Catalog,
			"params":           fields,
			"editor":           "plugin",
			"defaults":         sourceDefaults,
			"maxItems":         ls.MaxItems,
			"refresh":          ls.Refresh,
			"hint":             ls.Hint,
			"hubId":            pid,
			"rowKind":          pid,
			"collectionSource": pid,
			"sections":         []string{"home", "movies", "shows"},
		}
		dCol := extend.Descriptor{Kind: extend.KindCollectionSource, ID: pid, Owner: id, Label: textOf(id, ls.Label), Group: man.Name}
		dRow := extend.Descriptor{Kind: extend.KindRowSource, ID: pid, Owner: id, Label: textOf(id, ls.Label), Group: man.Name}
		if ls.Hint != "" {
			h := textOf(id, ls.Hint)
			dCol.Hint, dRow.Hint = h, h
		}
		out = append(out, dCol.WithMeta(meta), dRow.WithMeta(meta))
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapLiveTV) && c.Channels != nil {
		add(extend.KindLiveTVSource, "channels", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{
			"refresh": c.Channels.Refresh, "yieldsChannels": true, "yieldsGuide": true})
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapNotify) && c.Notification != nil {
		add(extend.KindChannelKind, "notify", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{
			"fields": notificationFields(id, c.Notification.Fields), "sendTest": c.Notification.SendTest, "selectable": true, "formats": c.Notification.Formats, "maxLength": c.Notification.MaxLength})
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapPluginDirectory) {
		for _, d := range c.Directories {
			add(extend.KindPluginDirectory, d.Key, textOf(id, d.Label), map[string]any{"key": d.Key})
		}
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapMetadata) && c.Metadata != nil {
		add(extend.KindMetadataProvider, "metadata", textOf(id, man.Name), c.Metadata)
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapSubtitles) && c.Subtitles != nil {
		add(extend.KindSubtitleProvider, "subtitles", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{
			"languages": c.Subtitles.Languages, "formats": c.Subtitles.Formats})
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapMarkers) && c.Markers != nil {
		add(extend.KindMarkerSource, "markers", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{"kinds": c.Markers.Kinds})
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapStreamSource) && c.Source != nil {
		add(extend.KindSourceKind, "stream", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{
			"class": c.Source.Class, "abilities": c.Source.Abilities, "limits": c.Source.Limits})
	}
	if man.HasCapability(CapDebridProvider) && c.Source != nil {
		add(extend.KindSourceKind, "debrid", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{"class": "debrid", "abilities": c.Source.Abilities})
	}
	if man.Ether.Kind == KindIntegration && c.Integration != nil {
		add(extend.KindIntegration, "integration", textOf(id, man.Name), map[string]any{
			"category": c.Integration.Category, "adds": c.Integration.Adds, "connect": c.Integration.Connect, "logo": c.Integration.Logo})
	}
	for _, tl := range c.Tools {
		add(extend.KindTool, tl.Name, textOf(id, tl.Title), map[string]any{
			"name": ToolName(id, tl.Name), "readOnly": tl.ReadOnly && man.RuntimeKind() == "hosted", "destructive": tl.Destructive, "openWorld": tl.OpenWorld})
	}
	return out
}
``````

``````
// ToolName namespaces a plugin tool for the catalogue: dots and dashes
// become underscores ("<plugin>__<name>").
func ToolName(plugin, name string) string {
	p := strings.NewReplacer(".", "_", "-", "_").Replace(plugin)
	return p + "__" + name
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/descriptors.go#*Manager.syncDescriptors

``````
// syncDescriptors replaces a plugin's registry descriptors and tools to
// match its record: none while disabled.
func (m *Manager) syncDescriptors(ctx context.Context, r Record) {
	if !r.Enabled {
		m.deps.OnAirContent.RemovePlugin(r.ID)
	} else {
		m.deps.OnAirContent.EnablePlugin(r.ID)
	}
	m.indexEventSubscriptions(r)
	m.syncNotificationKind(r)
	m.mu.Lock()
	m.shadow[r.ID] = r.Shadow
	m.mu.Unlock()
	if m.deps.Registry != nil {
		var ds []extend.Descriptor
		if r.Enabled {
			ds = DescriptorsFor(r.Manifest)
		}
		if err := m.deps.Registry.ReplaceOwner(r.ID, ds); err != nil {
			m.log.Warn("plugins: registry sync", "plugin", r.ID, "err", err)
		}
	}
	if m.deps.Tools != nil {
		var ts []tools.Tool
		if r.Enabled && r.Manifest.Ether != nil {
			for _, tl := range r.Manifest.Ether.Contributes.Tools {
				ts = append(ts, m.pluginTool(r, tl))
			}
		}
		if err := m.deps.Tools.ReplaceOwner(r.ID, ts); err != nil {
			m.log.Warn("plugins: tool sync", "plugin", r.ID, "err", err)
		}
	}
	m.mu.Lock()
	hooks := append([]func(context.Context, Record){}, m.syncHooks...)
	m.mu.Unlock()
	for _, fn := range hooks {
		fn(ctx, r)
	}
	m.prewarmHot(r)
}
``````
