// NewRankerTemplate builds a starter release-ranking step plugin.
func NewRankerTemplate(opts TemplateOptions) *Plugin {
	man := baseManifest(opts, KindExtension, []Capability{CapRankingStep})
	man.Ether.Settings = &SettingsSchema{
		Fields: []SettingField{{
			Key:     "boost4k",
			Kind:    "bool",
			Label:   "Boost 2160p releases",
			Default: true,
		}},
	}
	man.Ether.Contributes = &Contributes{
		RankingSteps: []RankingStepMeta{{
			Key:   "resolution_boost",
			Label: "Boost 2160p releases",
			Hint:  "Adds a score bonus when a candidate is 2160p",
		}},
	}
	return New(Definition{
		Manifest:        man,
		DefaultSettings: map[string]any{"boost4k": true},
		Routes: Routes{
			RankKey: func(candidate CandidateFacts, config map[string]any) int64 {
				var score int64
				if candidate.Cached {
					score += 500
				}
				boost4k, _ := config["boost4k"].(bool)
				is4k := candidate.Resolution == 2160 || candidate.Resolution == float64(2160) || candidate.Resolution == "2160p"
				if boost4k && is4k {
					score += 1000
				}
				return score
			},
		},
	})
}

func NewConditionTemplate(opts TemplateOptions) *Plugin {

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.DispatchTunnelFrame

``````
// DispatchTunnelFrame executes a `"request"` TunnelFrame against a Plugin and
// returns the outgoing response frames (either a single `"response"` frame or a
// `"response_start"` / `"response_chunk"` / `"response_end"` sequence for
// `/ether/file/*` binary responses).
func (p *Plugin) DispatchTunnelFrame(ctx context.Context, frame TunnelFrame, maxChunkBytes int) []TunnelFrame {
	if frame.Type != "request" || frame.ID == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if maxChunkBytes <= 0 {
		maxChunkBytes = DefaultMaxChunkBytes
	}

	var decodedBody []byte
	if frame.Body != "" {
		b, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(frame.Body)
		if err != nil {
			return []TunnelFrame{{
				Type:  "error",
				ID:    frame.ID,
				Error: &TunnelError{Code: "bad_request", Message: "Invalid base64 request body."},
			}}
		}
		decodedBody = b
	}

	hdrs := map[string]string{}
	for k, vals := range frame.Headers {
		if len(vals) > 0 {
			hdrs[k] = vals[0]
		}
	}
	if frame.RequestID != "" && hdrs["X-Ether-Request-ID"] == "" {
		hdrs["X-Ether-Request-ID"] = frame.RequestID
	}
	query := map[string]string{}
	for k, vals := range frame.Query {
		if len(vals) > 0 {
			query[k] = vals[0]
		}
	}

	res := p.Dispatch(ctx, RawRequest{
		Method:  frame.Method,
		Path:    frame.Path,
		Query:   query,
		Headers: hdrs,
		Body:    decodedBody,
	})

	multiHeaders := map[string][]string{}
	for k, v := range res.Headers {
		multiHeaders[k] = []string{v}
	}

	if res.BinaryBody != nil && strings.HasPrefix(frame.Path, "/ether/file/") {
		out := []TunnelFrame{{
			Type:    "response_start",
			ID:      frame.ID,
			Status:  res.Status,
			Headers: multiHeaders,
		}}
		limit := maxChunkBytes
		if limit < 1024 {
			limit = 1024
		}
		for offset := 0; offset < len(res.BinaryBody); offset += limit {
			end := offset + limit
			if end > len(res.BinaryBody) {
				end = len(res.BinaryBody)
			}
			out = append(out, TunnelFrame{
				Type: "response_chunk",
				ID:   frame.ID,
				Data: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(res.BinaryBody[offset:end]),
			})
		}
		out = append(out, TunnelFrame{
			Type: "response_end",
			ID:   frame.ID,
		})
		return out
	}

	payload := res.Body
	if res.BinaryBody != nil {
		payload = res.BinaryBody
	}
	var encodedBody string
	if len(payload) > 0 {
		encodedBody = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(payload)
	}
	return []TunnelFrame{{
		Type:    "response",
		ID:      frame.ID,
		Status:  res.Status,
		Headers: multiHeaders,
		Body:    encodedBody,
	}}
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.startTunnel

``````
func (p *Plugin) startTunnel(ctx context.Context, tunnelURL, credential string, fromFile bool, stateDir string) (*ServeHandle, error) {
	if tunnelURL == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("tunnel mode requires TunnelURL or ETHER_TUNNEL_URL")
	}
	loopCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	conn, maxChunk, err := p.dialTunnel(loopCtx, tunnelURL, credential)
	if err != nil {
		cancel()
		if errors.Is(err, errUnauthorized) && fromFile {
			clearSavedCredential(p.manifest.ID, stateDir)
			return nil, noCredentialError()
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		defer cancel()
		backoff := 100 * time.Millisecond
		for {
			started := time.Now()
			p.runTunnel(loopCtx, conn, maxChunk)
			if time.Since(started) >= time.Minute {
				backoff = 100 * time.Millisecond
			}
			for {
				// Equal jitter keeps retries bounded and avoids synchronized sidecars.
				delay := backoff/2 + time.Duration(rand.Int64N(int64(backoff/2)))
				timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
				select {
				case <-loopCtx.Done():
					timer.Stop()
					return
				case <-timer.C:
				}
				if backoff < 10*time.Second {
					backoff = min(backoff*2, 10*time.Second)
				}
				conn, maxChunk, err = p.dialTunnel(loopCtx, tunnelURL, credential)
				if err == nil {
					break
				}
				// A saved credential the server no longer accepts is dead:
				// clear it and stop rather than reconnect with it forever.
				if errors.Is(err, errUnauthorized) && fromFile {
					clearSavedCredential(p.manifest.ID, stateDir)
					return
				}
			}
		}
	}()
	return &ServeHandle{
		Done: done,
		Mode: "tunnel",
		URL:  tunnelURL,
		Close: func() error {
			cancel()
			<-done
			return nil
		},
	}, nil
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.dialTunnel

``````
// dialTunnel authenticates and completes the handshake on every attempt.
// Its timeout also bounds a peer that accepts a socket but never welcomes us.
func (p *Plugin) dialTunnel(ctx context.Context, tunnelURL, credential string) (*websocket.Conn, int, error) {
	handshakeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	dialOpts := &websocket.DialOptions{
		Subprotocols: []string{TunnelProtocol},
		HTTPHeader:   http.Header{},
	}
	if credential != "" {
		dialOpts.HTTPHeader.Set("X-Ether-Plugin-Credential", credential)
	}
	conn, resp, err := websocket.Dial(handshakeCtx, tunnelURL, dialOpts)
	if err != nil {
		if resp != nil {
			if resp.Body != nil {
				resp.Body.Close()
			}
			if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized {
				return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w (HTTP %d)", errUnauthorized, resp.StatusCode)
			}
		}
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	conn.SetReadLimit(16 << 20)
	helloBytes, _ := json.Marshal(TunnelFrame{
		Type: "hello", Protocol: TunnelProtocol, Plugin: p.manifest.ID,
		Features: []string{"range", "stream"},
	})
	if err := conn.Write(handshakeCtx, websocket.MessageText, helloBytes); err != nil {
		conn.CloseNow()
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	_, welcomeBytes, err := conn.Read(handshakeCtx)
	if err != nil {
		conn.CloseNow()
		return nil, 0, err
	}
	var welcome TunnelFrame
	if err := json.Unmarshal(welcomeBytes, &welcome); err != nil || welcome.Type != "welcome" {
		conn.CloseNow()
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("unexpected tunnel handshake response: %s", string(welcomeBytes))
	}
	maxChunk := welcome.MaxChunkBytes
	if maxChunk <= 0 {
		maxChunk = DefaultMaxChunkBytes
	}
	return conn, maxChunk, nil
}
``````

## Source: sdk/go/tunnel.go#*Plugin.runTunnel

``````
// runTunnel owns one socket. Only the supervisor dials; old handlers retain
// their old socket and are cancelled before a replacement is opened.
func (p *Plugin) runTunnel(ctx context.Context, conn *websocket.Conn, maxChunk int) {
	loopCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	defer cancel()
	defer conn.CloseNow()
	var mu sync.Mutex
	active := make(map[string]context.CancelFunc)
	defer func() {
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		for _, stop := range active {
			stop()
		}
	}()
	for {
		_, msgBytes, err := conn.Read(loopCtx)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		var frame TunnelFrame
		if json.Unmarshal(msgBytes, &frame) != nil {
			continue
		}
		if frame.Type == "cancel" {
			mu.Lock()
			stop := active[frame.ID]
			mu.Unlock()
			if stop != nil {
				stop()
			}
			continue
		}
		if frame.Type != "request" {
			continue
		}
		requestCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(loopCtx)
		mu.Lock()
		active[frame.ID] = stop
		mu.Unlock()
		go func(frame TunnelFrame) {
			defer func() { mu.Lock(); delete(active, frame.ID); mu.Unlock(); stop() }()
			for _, reply := range p.DispatchTunnelFrame(requestCtx, frame, maxChunk) {
				if requestCtx.Err() != nil {
					return
				}
				b, err := json.Marshal(reply)
				if err != nil {
					return
				}
				// WebSocket cancellation is connection-fatal. A per-request cancel
				// must stop dispatch, never interrupt a write on the shared socket.
				writeCtx, writeCancel := context.WithTimeout(loopCtx, 10*time.Second)
				err = conn.Write(writeCtx, websocket.MessageText, b)
				writeCancel()
				if err != nil {
					cancel()
					return
				}
			}
		}(frame)
	}
}
``````

``````
// EtherManifestBlock holds the EPP/1 `ether` manifest block.
type EtherManifestBlock struct {
	Protocol     int             `json:"protocol"`
	Kind         PluginKind      `json:"kind"`
	Capabilities []Capability    `json:"capabilities,omitempty"`
	Summary      string          `json:"summary"`
	Author       *PluginAuthor   `json:"author,omitempty"`
	License      string          `json:"license,omitempty"`
	Repo         string          `json:"repo,omitempty"`
	Icon         string          `json:"icon,omitempty"`

## Source: sdk/python/README.md

# `ether_plugin` (Python SDK)

Single-file, standard-library-only Python 3.9+ SDK for Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

## Features

- Zero external pip dependencies (`http.server`, `urllib.request`, `json`, `socket`, `base64`).
- Same declarative `plugin(manifest=..., routes=...)` router shape as `@ether/plugin-sdk` and `sdk/go`.
- Runs as an HTTP sidecar (`serve(p, mode="http")`) or an outbound WebSocket tunnel sidecar (`serve(p, mode="tunnel")`).
- Includes `RemoteHostClient` for `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential`, plus `create_test_harness`, `create_mock_host_client`, `fixtures`, and starter capability templates.

## Usage

```python
from ether_plugin import plugin, serve

hello = plugin(
    manifest={
        "id": "org.ether.examples.hello",
        "name": "Hello plugin",
        "version": "0.1.0",
        "description": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
        "types": ["movie"],
        "idPrefixes": ["tt"],
        "catalogs": [{"type": "movie", "id": "hello", "name": "Hello movies"}],
        "resources": ["catalog", "meta"],
        "ether": {
            "protocol": 1,
            "kind": "extension",
            "capabilities": ["list_source", "ui"],
            "summary": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
            "runtime": {"kind": "remote"},
        },
    },
    routes={
        "catalog": lambda req, ctx: {
            "metas": [
                {
                    "id": "tt0133093",
                    "type": req["type"],
                    "name": f"Hello from {req['id']}",
                    "releaseInfo": "1999",
                }
            ]
        },
    },
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(hello, background=False)
```

Tunnel mode makes one connection and returns when it drops. Use a process
supervisor to restart the sidecar after a disconnection.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket, so it needs no inbound
port. Pair once and the SDK saves the credential:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
python3 plugin.py
```

Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin › Connect a sidecar; it is
valid for 5 minutes and single use. `serve(plugin, mode="tunnel")` resolves the
credential in this order: an explicit credential, then the saved file, then the
pairing code (exchanged once and saved). With none it raises `CredentialError`
with one clear line.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base; the pair and `ws(s)` tunnel URLs
  are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else `~/.config/ether-plugins/<id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`). If the tunnel rejects a saved credential, the file is deleted and
`serve` raises `CredentialError` instead of reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY plugin.py ether_plugin.py manifest.json settings.schema.json ./
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
CMD ["python3", "plugin.py"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "command": "python3 plugin.py",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link.


Content-kind item dictionaries may include `unavailable: {"code": "no_verified_source",
"detail": "No verified source"}`. Ether keeps these items visible with the reason
and refuses resolution until a later upsert omits the field. `pattern: "file"`
with a `path` is reserved for hosted resolvers with `folders: read`; Python
sidecars cannot access host files or call `folders.hash`. See `docs/plugin-kinds.md`.

### Continuing background jobs

A `job` handler receives `{"name": ..., "continuation": ...}`. Return
`{"continueInMs": 0, "continuation": {"next": 41}, "progress": "Platform 41 of 92"}`
to continue. Return `{"done": True}` or `{"failed": "reason"}` to finish; an
absent `continueInMs` also finishes. Store durable checkpoints in KV to recover
on a later owner-started run after restart. Tokens are at most 64 KiB and progress
at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. The drawer supports progress and cancellation.

Ether uses owner-controlled global/per-plugin ceilings under Plugins: default
2 GiB memory (up to wasm32 4 GiB), 12 hours, effectively unlimited background
compute, 8 GiB downloads/member expansion, 32 GiB total expansion and 65,535 ZIP
members. Downloads also obey library cache quotas. Hosted manifests request
`ether.runtime.limits` with `memoryBytes`, `deadline`, `unitBudget`, `fetchBytes`,
`archiveMemberBytes`, `archiveExpandedBytes` and `archiveMembers`. Install preview
and detail show requested and granted values. Jobs pause during playback/high
host load and use low CPU/IO priority. A 1,000,000-call sanity bound applies;
viewer browse/search/resolve/playback calls retain tight time and compute budgets.
Remote Python processes manage their own CPU/memory. See the TypeScript SDK
README for route classification, policy APIs and complete job behavior.


## Source: sdk/python/ether_plugin.py

``````
"""Ether Plugin SDK for Python 3.9+ (stdlib-only, zero external dependencies).

Implements Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1) for sidecar and remote plugins:
- Declarative router (`plugin(manifest=..., routes=...)`) with identical route
  semantics to `@ether/plugin-sdk` and `sdk/go`.
- Settings schema decoding, validation, and copy-rule linting (SPEC §5.5).
- Localization helper (`create_i18n`, `t_ref`).
- Remote host client (`RemoteHostClient`) for `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated
  with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential` (SPEC §5.1.5, WS8b).
- HTTP sidecar server (`serve(..., mode="http")`) and WebSocket tunnel client
  (`serve(..., mode="tunnel")`, `dispatch_over_tunnel_frame`).
- Local test harness, mock host client, fixtures, and capability starter templates.
"""
